by: gazette session 4, step 5.3 (proposed; the integrator appends it)
title: An overseas company leaving New Zealand: its intention to cease to carry on business here, or its application for removal from the overseas register (Gazette section cb)

landmarks: the Gazette's own section code cb in the notice number (<year>-cb<n>): every notice so filed, and no other

signals_note: Recognised by the Gazette's classification, never by title words: the title is the company's name.
notes: Two shapes. notice: one overseas company, its name the title less the brackets that are not the name's own ('(New Zealand branch)', '(the "overseas company")', '(formerly …)', '(ACN …)'); the action from the notice's head: ceasing to carry on business in New Zealand (Companies Act 1993 s 343), or an application for removal from the overseas register; the 'Company No.' where the text prints exactly one; the day it ceases where printed; 'Dated'. list: the Registrar's 'Notice of Intention to Remove Overseas Companies From the Register', cut as the removal profile cuts its lists. No address is read.
applies_to: 2,607 notices, 2000 to 2026 (measured 20 October 2026: 2,601 read, 2,885 company rows, 95.4% held by the companies register)
process: Decide the shape.
Read the company from the title (or the list).
Read the action, section, number, the day it ceases and the Dated day.
gates: Every cb notice gives a company or is a catch-log line.
A title that is not a company's name, or a notice with no action the reader knows, is a catch-log line, never a guess.
on_fail: set aside the part or the notice; publish the rest

by: gazette session 4, step 5.3 (proposed; the integrator appends it)
title: The Registrar's notice of intention to restore companies or limited partnerships to the register (Gazette section ot)

landmarks: the Gazette's own section code ot in the notice number (<year>-ot<n>)
and 'restore' or 'restoration' in the title, or 'propose(s) to restore' or 'intend to restore' in the opening words

signals_note: Section ot ('companies: other') also holds prohibitions, amalgamations and the Registrar's rectifications; only the restorations are this profile. A restoration under ds stays with the removal profile.
notes: One shape: a list, one company or many, each followed by 'Applicant:' and the applicant's name and address. The applicant is often a person and the address often a home, so neither is read: each company is the text before an 'Applicant:', less everything up to the last comma that is not inside a name ('Able Company, Limited') and the address's closing town or postcode; the first is the longest end of the opening words after a stop that is a name and no prose. A number after the name is taken, behind the old registry office's two letters where printed ('AK. 123456'). The day objections close; 'Dated'; a court order restoring is said so.
applies_to: 888 notices, 2000 to 2026 (measured 20 October 2026: 868 read, 31,515 company rows, 93.1% held by the companies register; 166 rows a catch-log line)
process: Find the list by its 'Applicant:' markers.
Cut each company from the text before its applicant; never read the applicant.
Read the section, the objection day and the Dated day.
gates: Every ot notice titled a restoration gives a company or is a catch-log line.
A row that does not end in a legal suffix is a catch-log line, never a guess.
No applicant's name or address is held anywhere.
on_fail: set aside the part or the notice; publish the rest

by: gazette session 4, step 5.3 (proposed; the integrator appends it)
title: Incorporated societies and charitable trust boards dissolved, their dissolution revoked, or to be removed or restored (Gazette sections is and ct)

landmarks: the Gazette's own section code is or ct in the notice number

and a title of dissolution, revocation, intention to remove, restore or dissolve, or removal of societies or trusts; never a direction for the disposition of surplus assets, a scheme, a variation or financial statements

signals_note: Sections is and ct also hold directions on a dissolved body's surplus assets and applications to approve or vary charitable schemes; only the titles above are this profile.
notes: One shape: the Registrar's list. An opening sentence (ending at a colon, else at a stop after prose or the Act's year), then each body's name and its registration number, a revocation printing the day of the dissolution it undoes after the number '(3 May 2004)', the older lists 'Date of Dissolution: <day>' before the name; up to 'Dated', 'With this publication' or the Registrar's signature. A list that prints no numbers is cut at each bracketed day. The old registry office's letters after a name ('AK. I.S.', 'C.T.', 'WN') are dropped. A row that reads as prose is a catch-log line. The action: dissolution, revocation of dissolution, intention to dissolve (including a body's own request), intention to restore. The number is looked up in the societies' and trust boards' registers, never the companies'. No address is printed or read.
applies_to: 1,813 notices, 2000 to 2026 (measured 20 October 2026: 1,697 read, 33,749 body rows, 98.7% held by the register, 27,707 of 30,714 printed numbers agreeing by name)
process: Find where the list starts.
Cut each body at its number (or its bracketed day).
Read the action, section, each body's dissolution day where printed, and the Dated day.
gates: Every is or ct notice titled as above gives a body or is a catch-log line.
A row that reads as prose is a catch-log line, never a guess.
on_fail: set aside the part or the notice; publish the rest

by: gazette session 5, step 5.3 (proposed; the integrator appends it)
title: A mortgagee's notice of entry into possession of mortgaged land or goods, or of its receipt of the income (Gazette section gn; Property Law Act 2007 ss 156-157, 1952 Act s 92)

landmarks: the Gazette's own section code gn in the notice number
and 'possession', 'mortgaged land', 'mortgaged goods', 'mortgaged property' or 'receipt of income' in the title, or an entry into possession in the opening words; never a title of unclaimed property

signals_note: Section gn ('general') also holds unclaimed property, disciplinary findings and claims; only the titles and words above are this profile.
notes: No one form. The lender is read before '("the mortgagee")', ', the mortgagee' or ', as mortgagee', after 'the mortgagee' or 'Mortgagee's Full Name:', else as the subject of '... gives notice' or '... entered into possession', with its company number where printed. The borrower where printed: after 'the mortgagor', 'Mortgagor:', 'To:', 'granted by', 'in the matter of <company>', or before ', as mortgagor'. Land or goods from the title, else the text. The day of entry: 'with effect from', else the day in the sentence that enters, else the first 'on' or 'as from' day. The property (an address, often a home), the goods' description and their registration, VIN or serial numbers, and any person's name are private (gazette_private.possession_details) and never published; a title that names the property is published cut before it. A lender's name that may run on from the borrowers' ('in the matter of <persons> <lender>') is shown only as the end of it the companies register holds.
applies_to: 3,002 notices, 2000 to 2026 (measured 20 October 2026: 2,899 name their lender, 2,951 their day of entry; 2,449 of 2,864 company lenders held by the companies register, 85.5%; 103 notices a catch-log line)
process: Recognise by section and title or opening words.
Read the lender, the borrower, land or goods, the day of entry, the section and Dated.
Join the lender and a company borrower to the companies register; decide which names are shown.
gates: Every gn notice so titled is taken by the profile.
A notice with no lender the reader can name is a catch-log line, never a guess.
No property, registration number or person's name reaches a published row.
on_fail: set aside the part or the notice; publish the rest

title: The Registrar's notice of intention to rectify (correct) the New Zealand Register of Companies (Gazette section ot; Companies Act 1993 s 360A)

landmarks: the Gazette's own section code ot in the notice number
and 'correct the register' or 'rectify ... register' in the title or opening words

signals_note: Section ot ('companies: other') also holds prohibitions, restorations, the other three of the Registrar's notices read by gazette-5, extensions of time to register a charge, court applications and industrial and provident society notices; only the words above are this profile.
notes: One shape: a list of rows 'ACME LIMITED (in liquidation) (1234567) – <what the rectification does>', the older lists ending each row with its day and '(application by …)'. Each company is the capitals (or, in the older lists, the words ending in a legal suffix) before its bracketed number. What is corrected is kept only as words from a fixed list (director, shareholding, liquidation, receivership, administration, company name, annual return, address, constitution, amalgamation, removal or restoration, ultimate holding company, other), never the sentence. Each person a correction names (in set phrases: 'appointment of <name> as', 'that <name> was', '<name> as having ceased', 'the name of <name> was changed to'), and an applicant who is a person, is kept as initials and surname only; a name that does not reduce to that form is dropped. No address is read. The day objections close; 'Dated'.
process: Find the rows by their bracketed numbers.
Cut each company before its number.
Keep what is corrected as fixed words, the people and a person applicant as initials and surname.
gates: Every ot notice titled a correction of the register is taken by the profile.
A row whose company the reader cannot cut is a catch-log line.
No given name, no sentence of a correction and no address is held.

title: A proposal to amalgamate companies (Gazette section ot; Companies Act 1993 ss 219-221)

landmarks: the Gazette's own section code ot in the notice number
and 'amalgamat…' in the title or opening words, never a restoration

signals_note: Section ot ('companies: other') also holds prohibitions, restorations, the other three of the Registrar's notices read by gazette-5, extensions of time to register a charge, court applications and industrial and provident society notices; only the words above are this profile.
notes: No one form; the title is often the companies' names. Every company the title and the operative words name (up to 'Copies of the amalgamation proposal', 'available for inspection', 'registered office' or 'Dated'), once each, the words before each legal suffix; the one the notice says continues ('X will continue as the amalgamated company', 'X continuing as the amalgamated company', 'which shall become the amalgamated company', 'the amalgamated company will be X') marked 'amalgamated company', the rest 'amalgamating company'. Many notices form a new company and name none to continue: a catch-log line, the companies kept. The day it takes effect where printed; 'Dated'. Directors' signatures and addresses are not read.
process: Take the companies from the title and the operative words.
Mark the one that continues.
Read the day it takes effect and Dated.
gates: Every ot notice titled an amalgamation is taken by the profile.
A notice naming no company is a catch-log line.

title: A company's notice of intention to be removed from the New Zealand register on becoming incorporated elsewhere (Gazette section ot; Companies Act 1993 s 343)

landmarks: the Gazette's own section code ot in the notice number
and a transfer of registration or incorporation, 'by transfer', 'other jurisdiction' or 'removed from the New Zealand register in connection with' in the title or opening words

signals_note: Section ot ('companies: other') also holds prohibitions, restorations, the other three of the Registrar's notices read by gazette-5, extensions of time to register a charge, court applications and industrial and provident society notices; only the words above are this profile.
notes: One company: the title's name, else the name before 'gives notice', else the first name the opening words print. Where it goes: the words after 'incorporated under the law in force in'. The day after which it applies; 'Dated'. Signatures not read.
process: Take the company.
Read where it goes and the day after which it applies.
gates: Every ot notice titled a transfer is taken by the profile.
A notice naming no company is a catch-log line.

title: A deed of company arrangement executed, varied or ended (Gazette section ot; Companies Act 1993 Part 15A)

landmarks: the Gazette's own section code ot in the notice number
and 'deed of company arrangement' in the title or opening words

signals_note: Section ot ('companies: other') also holds prohibitions, restorations, the other three of the Registrar's notices read by gazette-5, extensions of time to register a charge, court applications and industrial and provident society notices; only the words above are this profile.
notes: The company from the title (the status bracket '(subject to deed of company arrangement)' dropped), else the opening words; the action (executed, varied, terminated, a notice to creditors); the day after 'On'; the deed administrators as signed ('…, Deed Administrators'), as the administrators are read. No address or telephone is read.
process: Take the company and the action.
Read the day and the deed administrators as signed.
gates: Every ot notice titled a deed of company arrangement is taken by the profile.
A notice naming no company is a catch-log line.
